context.audience: Tier 1 OEM brand/awareness planners, Tier 2 regional dealer association media buyers, Tier 3 individual franchise dealer operators. Secondary audiences include in-market car shoppers (72-day average consideration window), in-service/parts buyers, and fleet/commercial vehicle purchasers.
pain_points: Dealer co-op budget reconciliation — OEM sets approved channel lists and reimbursement rules, but tier 2/3 execution requires dealers to spend first and claim back, creating cash-flow friction and compliance audits

Tier conflict in paid search: OEM national campaigns, regional dealer group campaigns, and individual dealer campaigns all bid against each other on the same branded and model-specific keywords, inflating CPCs across the system

Attribution of test-drive and showroom visits back to specific digital touchpoints — the path from CTV impression to lot visit spans 8–12 weeks and multiple devices, making last-click models highly misleading

Managing model-year changeover campaigns: overlapping 'clearance of current year' and 'conquest for new model year' messaging requires precision geo-targeting and audience suppression to avoid cannibalizing each other

Inventory volatility disrupting always-on media plans — chip shortage cycles, electrification model launches, and regional supply imbalances force constant mid-flight budget reallocation across dealers and DMAs
EV-specific media strategy requires distinct audience segmentation (early adopter vs. range-anxious mainstream buyer) and channel mix separate from ICE conquest campaigns
kpis: Vehicle Detail Page (VDP) views per campaign dollar — primary measure of digital inventory engagement
Cost per showroom visit / test-drive booking (offline conversion via store visit measurement)
Cost per qualified lead (CPL) from form fills, phone calls, and chat on dealer sites
Share of voice (SOV) vs. competitor brands in-market within the DMA
Brand health metrics: unaided awareness, purchase consideration, conquest rate vs. competitive set
Dealer co-op fund utilization rate (% of eligible funds actually claimed and deployed)
Average days-to-sale and inventory turn velocity linked to media flight periods
context.regulatory: No direct pharmaceutical-style ad restrictions, but dealer advertising is heavily governed by FTC truth-in-advertising rules on pricing disclosures, APR/lease terms (TILA/Regulation Z), and state dealer licensing laws. OEM co-op programs must comply with Robinson-Patman Act (equitable dealer access). EV advertising increasingly scrutinized for range claim accuracy. Political broadcast adjacency standards apply on linear TV.
context.seasonality: Tax refund season (Feb–Apr) drives highest volume for value/entry segments. Memorial Day, Labor Day, and Black Friday 'tent-pole' sales events require 4–6-week media build. Model-year-end clearance peaks August–September. December traditionally largest single month for luxury and near-luxury due to 'Season of Sales' campaigns. Winter/summer tire and service campaigns create secondary media windows for dealers.
context.budget_dynamics: US automotive advertising reached $39.5B globally in 2025. Dealer-level digital now commands 65%+ of spend, up from ~40% five years ago. CTV is the fastest-growing channel, with 61% of car shoppers reporting CTV influenced their purchase decision. Paid search remains the workhorse (highest intent, highest CPCs). Shift underway from OEM-controlled national TV to dealer-addressable CTV+programmatic. Average franchise dealer spends $529K/year on advertising (NADA 2023). Co-op accrual models mean 50–70% of dealer digital spend is partially OEM-subsidized.
channels_that_work: Paid search (Google/Bing) — captures in-market intent on model, trim, and financing queries; highest conversion channel despite $15–40 CPCs in competitive markets
Connected TV (CTV/OTT) — growing fastest for both OEM brand and dealer local; 61% purchase influence rate; allows geo-fencing by DMA with VIN-level inventory dynamic creative
Programmatic display with first-party DMS/CRM data — retargeting site visitors against specific inventory pages; lookalike modeling off past buyer data
Social (Meta + TikTok) — Meta Lead Ads for test-drive requests effective for under-35 buyers; TikTok growing for EV awareness among younger demographics
Third-party automotive platforms (Autotrader, Cars.com, KBB) — high-intent in-market inventory listings; Autotrader/KBB Alpha Ads for conquest positioning
Linear TV — still used by OEMs for national reach/brand events (Super Bowl, model launches); declining at dealer tier
Streaming audio (Spotify, Pandora) — drive-time commuter targeting; highest ROI-rated format among dealership stakeholders per Statista
measurement_challenges: Cross-device attribution across an 8–12 week purchase funnel with 8–10 touchpoints; store visit measurement varies significantly by vendor methodology
Co-op compliance reporting — verifying that dealer-level spend meets OEM creative standards and channel eligibility rules for reimbursement without a unified dashboard
Separating incremental sales lift from seasonality and inventory availability effects when running always-on campaigns
VDP-to-lead-to-sale funnel leakage: 70%+ of high-intent VDP visitors never submit a form, making visit-based attribution incomplete
EV conversion attribution: test-drive incentives, state rebate announcements, and charging infrastructure proximity all interact with media exposure in ways standard MTA models cannot isolate
subtopics: OEM national brand and model launch media planning
Dealer co-op program management and compliance
Tier 2 regional dealer association media coordination
EV and alternative powertrain conquest media strategy
Automotive paid search architecture (OEM vs. dealer keyword conflict)
In-market audience targeting and VDP retargeting
CTV and streaming video for automotive dealers
Service lane and aftersales media (parts, maintenance, accessories)
context.typical_budget_range: Franchise dealer: $400K–$1.2M/year. Regional dealer group (20–50 points): $5M–$25M/year. OEM Tier 1 national: $500M–$2B+/year (Ford, GM, Stellantis). Tier 2 regional ad association: $10M–$80M/year depending on market.
context.buying_model: Highly fragmented across tiers. OEM Tier 1: primarily upfront/scatter broadcast TV, programmatic guaranteed, direct publisher deals. Tier 2: mix of linear TV, programmatic display, and search. Tier 3 (dealers): predominantly self-serve or agency-managed programmatic, paid search via platforms like Dealer.com, PureCars, or Dealers United. Co-op funding flows from OEM to dealer via accrual percentage of vehicle invoice, claimed against pre-approved media buys.
context.creative_considerations: Vehicle imagery quality is paramount — lifestyle context (road, terrain, family) must match model positioning. Dealers require localized price/incentive call-outs compliant with OEM co-op rules (APR disclosures, MSRP vs. dealer pricing). CTV creative must work in 15s and 30s with logo/CTA visible in first 5 seconds before skip. EV campaigns must address range anxiety and charging accessibility with specificity. Dynamic creative optimization (DCO) needed to swap in VIN-specific inventory images at scale.
